MATHEMATICS — MOCK EXAM #15
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: MATHEMATICS
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which digit holds a place in 6,092 even though it is worth nothing? (1 mark)
   A. 6
   B. 0
   C. 2
   D. 9

2. Which number is written in words as "five thousand, three hundred"? (1 mark)
   A. 530
   B. 53,000
   C. 5,030
   D. 5,300

3. Which list shows all the factors of 18? (1 mark)
   A. 1, 2, 3, 6, 9
   B. 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18
   C. 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 18
   D. 1, 2, 6, 9, 18

4. Which list shows all the factors of 24? (1 mark)
   A. 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 12, 24
   B. 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24
   C. 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24
   D. 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12

5. Work out 4,750 + 3,895. (1 mark)
   A. 8,645
   B. 8,545
   C. 7,545
   D. 8,655

6. Estimate 4,368 + 2,547 by rounding each number to the nearest ten. (1 mark)
   A. 7,015
   B. 6,920
   C. 6,910
   D. 6,930

7. Which sum checks that 6,003 − 2,475 = 3,528? (1 mark)
   A. 6,003 + 2,475
   B. 6,003 + 3,528
   C. 3,528 + 2,475
   D. 3,528 − 2,475

8. Which pattern has the rule multiply by 2? (1 mark)
   A. 5, 10, 15, 20
   B. 2, 4, 6, 8
   C. 3, 5, 7, 9
   D. 2, 4, 8, 16

9. Every product in the 5 times table ends in (1 mark)
   A. 2 or 7
   B. 5 or 9
   C. 0 or 5
   D. 1 or 6

10. Work out 18 × 35. (1 mark)
   A. 144
   B. 620
   C. 630
   D. 640

11. Estimate 24 × 18 by rounding each number to the nearest ten. (1 mark)
   A. 500
   B. 400
   C. 4,000
   D. 300

12. Which division fact belongs to the same family as 9 × 5 = 45? (1 mark)
   A. 5 ÷ 9 = 45
   B. 45 ÷ 9 = 5
   C. 45 ÷ 45 = 9
   D. 45 ÷ 9 = 9

13. Change 7/3 to a mixed fraction. (1 mark)
   A. 1 2/3
   B. 3 1/3
   C. 2 1/3
   D. 2 2/3

14. Ali writes another set of fractions. Which of these is a mixed fraction? (1 mark)
   A. 8/3
   B. 3/8
   C. 1 3/4
   D. 7/4

15. Change 1 5/6 to an improper fraction. (1 mark)
   A. 12/6
   B. 6/6
   C. 11/6
   D. 11/7

16. What is 2/3 of 21? (1 mark)
   A. 21
   B. 14
   C. 5
   D. 7

17. A hundred square has 48 of its small squares shaded. Which decimal shows the shaded part? (1 mark)
   A. 0.048
   B. 48
   C. 0.48
   D. 4.8

18. In the number 9.27, the digit 7 is in which place? (1 mark)
   A. Tens
   B. Hundredths
   C. Tenths
   D. Ones

19. If a = 5, what is the value of a + 7? (1 mark)
   A. 12
   B. 2
   C. 35
   D. 57

20. If b = 3, what is the value of 2b + 1? (1 mark)
   A. 21
   B. 6
   C. 7
   D. 5

21. Change 2 m 45 cm to centimetres. (1 mark)
   A. 65 cm
   B. 2,450 cm
   C. 245 cm
   D. 47 cm

22. A fence uses 3 pieces of wire, each 1 m 25 cm long. What is the total length of wire? (1 mark)
   A. 3 m 75 cm
   B. 1 m 28 cm
   C. 3 m 65 cm
   D. 4 m 75 cm

23. What is 7 m 5 cm − 1 m 48 cm? (1 mark)
   A. 5 m 67 cm
   B. 5 m 57 cm
   C. 5 m 47 cm
   D. 6 m 57 cm

24. What is 3.4 m in centimetres? (1 mark)
   A. 340 cm
   B. 3,400 cm
   C. 304 cm
   D. 34 cm

25. Which sum finds the area of a rectangle with 4 rows and 6 columns? (1 mark)
   A. 4 + 6
   B. 4 × 6
   C. 4 − 6
   D. 6 ÷ 4

26. A cuboid is 6 blocks long, 4 blocks wide and 3 blocks high. What is its volume? (1 mark)
   A. 13 blocks
   B. 24 blocks
   C. 78 blocks
   D. 72 blocks

27. What is 5 h 20 min − 2 h 35 min? (1 mark)
   A. 2 h 35 min
   B. 2 h 55 min
   C. 2 h 45 min
   D. 3 h 45 min

28. In which direction do shadows point in the early morning? (1 mark)
   A. Towards the east
   B. Straight up
   C. They do not point anywhere
   D. Towards the west

29. One unit costs Ksh 45. What is the cost of 5 mandazi? (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 235
   B. Ksh 50
   C. Ksh 225
   D. Ksh 180

30. An angle that is bigger than a right angle has arms that are (1 mark)
   A. joined into one line and closed
   B. closer together than a right angle
   C. further apart than the arms of a right angle
   D. exactly the same as a right angle

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. A stack of soda crates has 5 crates along the wall, 4 crates deep and 4 layers high. How many crates are in the stack? (3 marks)

32. Give two things you should do to stay safe when you collect data about vehicles. (2 marks)

33. Add 2 hours 45 minutes and 1 hour 30 minutes. (3 marks)

34. Wanjiru buys goods worth Ksh 750 and pays with a Ksh 1,000 note. How much change should she get? Check your answer. (3 marks)

35. A trip leaves at 7:45 a.m. and takes 2 hours 30 minutes. At what time does it arrive? (3 marks)

36. Draw a triangle and write down its number of sides and corners. (2 marks)

37. A school tank held 8,500 litres of water. The school used 3,275 litres in the first week and 1,850 litres in the second week. How much water is left? Check your answer. (5 marks)

38. A rectangle has an area of 48 square units and 6 rows. How many columns does it have? Explain how you found out. (3 marks)

39. The table shows football 5, netball 3, athletics 1 and swimming 1 for 10 pupils. Which sport is the most popular? How many pupils chose netball or athletics? (3 marks)

40. Kip faces west and makes a quarter turn clockwise. Which way does he face now? Explain. (3 marks)

41. Find 3/4 of 12 counters. Explain each step. (3 marks)

42. One layer of a cuboid has 15 blocks and the cuboid has 4 layers. Find the volume. Then find the volume if 2 more layers are added. (4 marks)

43. Work out 12 × 21 showing both partial products. (3 marks)

44. Change Ksh 12 to cents and 1,250 cents to shillings. (2 marks)

45. Wanjiru studied for 1 hour 20 minutes on Monday and 45 minutes on Tuesday. How long did she study in all? (3 marks)

46. Describe a pattern of shapes that you can make with squares and triangles, and write down the first six shapes. (3 marks)

47. Name two things at home or school that are turned clockwise to tighten or close them. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
MATHEMATICS — MOCK EXAM #15 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — 0
   The zero shows that there are no hundreds. Without it the number would be 692.

2. D — 5,300
   five thousand, three hundred: put each part in its place and use 0 where there is no digit. The number is 5,300.

3. B — 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18
   Pair up numbers that multiply to 18. The factors are 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18.

4. C — 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24
   Pair up numbers that multiply to 24. The factors are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24.

5. A — 8,645
   Add ones, tens, hundreds and thousands, regrouping when a column is 10 or more. 4,750 + 3,895 = 8,645.

6. B — 6,920
   4,368 rounds to 4,370 and 2,547 rounds to 2,550. 4,370 + 2,550 = 6,920.

7. C — 3,528 + 2,475
   Addition undoes subtraction. 3,528 + 2,475 = 6,003, the starting number.

8. D — 2, 4, 8, 16
   2 × 2 = 4, 4 × 2 = 8, 8 × 2 = 16. The other patterns add 2 or add 5.

9. C — 0 or 5
   5, 10, 15, 20, 25 ... All end in 0 or 5.

10. C — 630
   18 × 5 = 90 and 18 × 30 = 540. 90 + 540 = 630.

11. B — 400
   24 rounds to 20 and 18 rounds to 20. 20 × 20 = 400.

12. B — 45 ÷ 9 = 5
   Division undoes multiplication. Since 9 × 5 = 45, we know 45 ÷ 9 = 5 and 45 ÷ 5 = 9.

13. C — 2 1/3
   7 ÷ 3 = 2 remainder 1. The whole number is 2 and the fraction is 1/3, so 7/3 = 2 1/3.

14. C — 1 3/4
   A mixed fraction has a whole number and a proper fraction, like 1 3/4.

15. C — 11/6
   1 × 6 = 6 and 6 + 5 = 11. The denominator stays 6, so the answer is 11/6.

16. B — 14
   21 ÷ 3 = 7 and 7 × 2 = 14. So 2/3 of 21 is 14.

17. C — 0.48
   48 out of 100 squares is 48/100 = 0.48.

18. B — Hundredths
   The first digit after the decimal point is tenths and the second is hundredths. In 9.27 the digit 7 is in the hundredths place.

19. A — 12
   Replace the letter by its value and work it out. The answer is 12.

20. C — 7
   Replace the letter by its value and work it out. The answer is 7.

21. C — 245 cm
   1 m = 100 cm. 2 × 100 = 200, and 200 + 45 = 245. So the answer is 245 cm.

22. A — 3 m 75 cm
   125 × 3 = 375 cm = 3 m 75 cm.

23. B — 5 m 57 cm
   705 − 148 = 557 cm = 5 m 57 cm.

24. A — 340 cm
   1 m = 100 cm. Use this to change between the two units: 3.4 m in centimetres is 340 cm.

25. B — 4 × 6
   Area is the number of rows multiplied by the number of columns.

26. D — 72 blocks
   One layer has 6 × 4 = 24 blocks. There are 3 layers, so the volume is 24 × 3 = 72 blocks.

27. C — 2 h 45 min
   Change 1 hour to 60 minutes when the minutes are not enough. The answer is 2 h 45 min.

28. D — Towards the west
   The Sun rises in the east, so morning shadows point west.

29. C — Ksh 225
   Cost = number × price = 5 × 45 = Ksh 225.

30. C — further apart than the arms of a right angle
   A bigger angle has arms opened wider than a square corner.

SECTION B
----
31. (3 marks)
   Answer: 80 crates
   Working / marking points: 5 × 4 = 20 per layer (1 mark); 20 × 4 (1 mark); 80 crates (1 mark).

32. (2 marks)
   Answer: Count from a safe place inside the school gate and stay with a teacher. Do not stand in or near the road.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sensible safety rule.

33. (3 marks)
   Answer: 4 hours 15 minutes
   Working / marking points: 45 + 30 = 75 min and 2 + 1 = 3 h (1 mark); 75 min = 1 h 15 min (1 mark); total 4 h 15 min (1 mark).

34. (3 marks)
   Answer: Ksh 250. Check: 750 + 250 = 1,000.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 1,000 − 750, 1 mark for Ksh 250, 1 mark for the check.

35. (3 marks)
   Answer: 10:15 a.m.
   Working / marking points: 7:45 + 2 h = 9:45 (1 mark); 9:45 + 30 min = 10:15 (1 mark); a.m. stated (1 mark).

36. (2 marks)
   Answer: A drawing of a triangle with 3 straight sides. It has 3 sides and 3 corners.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the drawing and 1 mark for the numbers.

37. (5 marks)
   Answer: 3,375 litres
   Working / marking points: 8,500 − 3,275 = 5,225 (2 marks); 5,225 − 1,850 = 3,375 (2 marks); check by adding 3,375 + 1,850 + 3,275 = 8,500 (1 mark).

38. (3 marks)
   Answer: 8 columns. Area = rows × columns, so columns = 48 ÷ 6 = 8.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the relationship, 1 mark for the division, 1 mark for 8.

39. (3 marks)
   Answer: Football is the most popular. 3 + 1 = 4 pupils chose netball or athletics.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for football, 1 mark for 3 + 1, 1 mark for 4.

40. (3 marks)
   Answer: North
   Working / marking points: Going clockwise the order is N, E, S, W and back to N (1 mark). West then a quarter turn clockwise gives north (1 mark). Answer north (1 mark).

41. (3 marks)
   Answer: 9 counters. 12 ÷ 4 = 3 counters in one quarter; 3 × 3 = 9.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for dividing by the denominator, 1 mark for multiplying by the numerator, 1 mark for the answer.

42. (4 marks)
   Answer: 60 blocks; then 90 blocks
   Working / marking points: 15 × 4 = 60 (2 marks); 6 layers: 15 × 6 = 90 (2 marks).

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: 252
   Working / marking points: 12 × 1 = 12 (1 mark); 12 × 20 = 240 (1 mark); 12 + 240 = 252 (1 mark).

44. (2 marks)
   Answer: Ksh 12 = 1,200 cents; 1,250 cents = Ksh 12.50
   Working / marking points: 12 × 100 = 1,200 (1 mark); 1,250 ÷ 100 = 12 remainder 50, so Ksh 12.50 (1 mark).

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: 2 hours 5 minutes
   Working / marking points: 20 + 45 = 65 min (1 mark); 1 h + 65 min = 2 h 5 min (2 marks).

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example: square, triangle, square, triangle, square, triangle. The pattern repeats a square and a triangle in turn.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for using both shapes, 1 mark for a clear repeating rule, 1 mark for six correct shapes.

47. (2 marks)
   Answer: Any two, for example a bottle top or a screw, and a tap being closed.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct example.
